full_text:
Hansel was a gambler who played cards and rolled dice from dawn till dusk, losing his coat, his boots, and his father's cottage, yet his cheerful passion for gaming never diminished.

When he gave shelter to a wandering pilgrim, he was granted a magical apple tree from which no one could climb down without Hansel's permission, and a deck of cards that never lost a wager.

When Death came with his scythe to take Hansel away, Hansel said courteously: "Dear Death, before we depart, would you kindly climb my apple tree and pick me one sweet apple for the journey?"

Death climbed into the tree, and immediately became stuck fast to the boughs! For seven long years, Death sat trapped in the tree; no one on earth died, no sickness was fatal, and humanity lived in endless merriment.

Finally, Hansel bargained with Death: he would release him only if Death promised never to claim him until Hansel called for him.

Years later, when Hansel wearied of mortal life, he journeyed to the underworld, pulled out his magical cards, and won games against every spirit in the halls, winning countless souls and leading them in a joyful procession straight into paradise, proving that an unyielding spirit laughs at fate itself.
moral: Sharp wits that refuse defeat can turn even the final judgment into a spirited game of dice.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Gambling Hansel variant"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
